title: A Birthday Mystery!
text: Imagine your best friend just moved to a different city far, far away. Today is their birthday! You want to wish them a very 'Happy Birthday', but you cannot travel to their city today. What will you do?

title: Think About It...
text: Can you think of all the different ways you can send a message to someone who is far away? If you don't have a phone, how else could they hear from you?

content.title: The Journey of a Message!
content.description: Watch how messages travel! First, a flying pigeon, then a postman carrying a letter, then a ringing telephone, and finally a fast email!

title: What is Communication?
text: Sharing our thoughts, ideas, or news with other people is called **Communication**. When we speak, write, or even use our hands to wave 'Hello', we are communicating!

content.meaning: The act of sharing thoughts, ideas, and information with others.

title: Means of Communication
text: We have many tools to help us communicate. We can write letters (sent through a post office), talk on a telephone or mobile phone, or send emails using the internet.

content.meaning: A global computer network providing a variety of information and communication facilities.

content.question: If you want to quickly talk to your grandmother who lives in another town, what is the best thing to use?

title: A Look Back in Time
text: Think about it! A long time ago, before phones were invented, people used trained pigeons or men on horses to carry letters. Imagine how many days or weeks it would take just to say 'Hello'!

content.tip: Ask your parents or grandparents how they used to send urgent messages when they were your age. Did they use telegrams or postcards?

title: Talking to Many People at Once!
text: Sometimes, one person wants to send a message to thousands of people at the same time. This is called **Mass Communication**. Newspapers, radio, and television help us do this! When you watch the news on TV, that is Mass Communication.

content.meaning: Sending information to a very large number of people at the same time, like through TV or newspapers.

content.title: The Power of Mass Media
content.description: One TV tower sending invisible signals to thousands of homes so everyone can watch the same show together!

content.title: Your Own Postcard!
content.description: Take a piece of paper and draw a picture on one side. On the other side, write a short message to your best friend. Put a stamp on it (or draw one) and you have made a postcard!

content.mistake: Thinking that shouting loudly to someone far away is a good way to communicate.
content.correction: Shouting can hurt your throat and the other person might not hear you correctly! Using a phone or writing a letter is a much better and clearer way to send your message.

content.question: Which of these is a way to communicate with many people at the same time (Mass Communication)?
options: A telephone call to a friend
